title: A longitudinal observational study of patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and healthy control subjects to analyse the relationship between the menstrual cycle, psychosocial factors and the course of IBD.
summary:
Women with IBD report changing symptoms during their menstrual cycle. It is unclear however exactly how the hormone cycle influences the course of the disease.
The CARMEN study therefore aims to understand the influence of the female cycle on the well-being and symptoms of patients. The timing and influence of medication intake will also be investigated. Another focus is on the connection between IBD and cycle-dependent symptoms such as PMS or premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD). Further psychosocial aspects are also taken into account.
conditions: Inflammatory Bowel Diseases (IBD), Crohn´s disease, Ulcerative Colitis

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Pre-existing inflammatory bowel disease (> 3 months).
Active menstrual cycle (at least 3 menstrual periods during the past 6 months).
Remission to moderate disease activity (HBI <17 points; SCCAI <12 points).
Written consent of the patient after receiving full information.
Exclusion criteria:
Conditions that prevent the subject from understanding the nature and implications of the clinical trial and its possible consequences.
Male sex.
Known menopause.
Pregnancy.
Hormonal contraception.
